bull.b: The sharp revenue rebound and higher gross margin indicate improving demand and better unit economics. If sustained, this recovery can provide operating leverage and strengthen the business after several years of volatile results.

The shift from heavy cash burn to positive operating and free cash flow is a constructive fundamental inflection. Although the cushion remains small, continued cash generation could reduce reliance on external financing.

Recent quarterly improvement across revenue, gross profit, operating performance, and equity suggests the recovery is extending beyond a single income-statement line. Sustained execution could gradually improve financial resilience.

bear.b: The company remains loss-making despite the revenue rebound, while modest EBITDA leaves little protection if demand or margins weaken. The history of losses limits confidence that the current recovery is durable.

Debt remains slightly above equity and materially constrains financial flexibility, even after improving from 2025. Elevated leverage increases refinancing and downside risk if the cyclical steel business experiences weaker margins.

The ATM facility provides needed financing flexibility but creates a durable risk of share dilution while profitability and free cash flow remain weak. Funding operations through equity could also limit per-share recovery potential.
